security_audit.summary: All 400 presented findings were adjudicated; most are defensive checks, Python syntax, documentation, or local metadata handling. User-authority provider and verifier execution, ambient hooks, and broad native Keychain authority remain real risks; no evidence found of deliberate malware or audit manipulation. The analyzer capped review at 400 of 680 matches; the remaining 280 require manual adjudication before automatic publication. Static review was capped at 400/680 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 280 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Session providers retain normal host filesystem and network authority.
remediation.suggestion: Require an isolated execution environment for untrusted tasks, or make session exposure a separate explicit approval. Never present staging as host isolation.

remediation.issue: Ordinary verification executes untrusted candidate code with user authority.
remediation.suggestion: Run verifiers in disposable OS-isolated environments with denied network access and no credentials. Repository snapshots cannot replace filesystem isolation.

remediation.issue: Ambient user hooks and plugins are outside the approved task-content binding.
remediation.suggestion: Use a dedicated provider profile without ambient executable configuration. Otherwise require explicit review of enabled hooks and plugins before each session launch.

remediation.issue: Native Keychain helper authority is not restricted to provider authentication operations.
remediation.suggestion: Replace general helper access with an operation-specific credential broker or dedicated provider-only credential store. Keep unrelated user Keychain items inaccessible.

remediation.issue: The static review omitted 280 repeated or lower-priority matches.
remediation.suggestion: Submit the remaining matches for contextual adjudication before enabling automatic publication.

content.user_title: Delegate Repository Tasks and Verify Results
content.value_statement: Delegated coding work needs clear content approval and independent checks. agy-worker coordinates Antigravity CLI tasks through scoped staging, bounded repairs, candidate review, and recorded verification.
actual_capabilities: Preview provider-readable content and bind the exact task and launch settings to an approval digest.
Stage selected read paths and reconcile changes only within an approved write subset.
Coordinate explore, task, and project workflows with cycle limits and local job status.
Preserve candidate changes and support approved repairs within the same worker conversation.
Create verification copies and bind driver-selected checks to candidate state before finalization.
Offer explicit native containment for supported macOS scoped jobs without silently falling back to session mode.
limitations: Requires Bash, Python 3, Git, and an installed Antigravity CLI with provider access for live tasks.
Session mode is not host isolation and can load ambient user hooks or plugins.
Native containment is limited to supported macOS scoped jobs and retains documented network and Keychain limitations.
Worker reports and passing gates do not prove correctness; ordinary verifier execution still requires a trusted or separately isolated environment.

best_practices: Review exact task content, readable paths, model, isolation mode, and budgets before approving the launch digest.
Keep secrets, raw logs, controller state, and private verification manifests outside provider-readable content.
Inspect candidate diffs and run driver-owned checks in a separately isolated verification environment before finalization.
anti_patterns: Treating installation, an approval digest, or a worker success report as permission for unrelated actions.
Assuming scoped staging or a disposable Git worktree prevents session-mode host access.
Executing commands copied from worker reports or accepting candidates without independent review.

faq.question: Which driver tools are supported?
faq.answer: The package supports Codex CLI and Claude Code as drivers. Antigravity CLI performs delegated provider work.

faq.question: Does installing the skill authorize provider transmission?
faq.answer: No. Each launch needs approval for its exact task, readable content, destination, isolation mode, model, and budget.

faq.question: What does scoped dispatch restrict?
faq.answer: It stages selected readable paths and limits reconciled writes. In session mode, it does not restrict the provider's host filesystem or network authority.

faq.question: Does a ready diagnostic prove authentication?
faq.answer: No. Offline readiness checks prerequisites, not provider authentication, model availability, or future job success.

faq.question: Can the worker run its own acceptance commands?
faq.answer: Worker command claims are not executed or accepted as evidence. Optional self-verification provides advisory feedback; the driver selects checks and owns acceptance.

faq.question: Is native isolation available on every platform?
faq.answer: No. Native isolation requires supported macOS scoped containment and compatible host sandbox settings. It does not silently fall back to session mode.
